name: hardware-mixed-consumables
derivation: base lines 200/10/0/1000/0 (consumables $2.10). Magnet $1.00 x 2 = $2.00 (lostOnFailure) -> failureBase $2.10 + $2.00 = $4.10, failure 10% = $0.41 (41c). Hook $0.50 x 1 = $0.50, never in the base. perUnitTotal 200+10+0+41+1000+0+200+50 = 1501; batchTotal x1 = 1501. Failure buffer is base x p / (1 - p).

name: hardware-pricing-markup-tax-fees-qty2
derivation: Hardware inside a FULL pricing block (markup strategy, quantity 2, non-zero tax/shipping/fees) -- the existing hardware+pricing coverage used a 30% margin at quantity 1 with all three zeroed. batch labor $10.00/2 = $5.00 (500c); failure base $2.10 + $2.00 = $4.10 -> 41c; perUnitTotal 200+10+0+41+500+0+200 = 951; batchTotal 951x2 = 1902. markup x2 -> recommended = resolved = 1902. itemRevenue 1902x2 = 3804, + shipping 500 -> revenue 4304. fees: $0.50 fixed = 50 and 10% of 4304 = roundCents(430.4) = 430 -> 480. tax price-inclusive on item revenue only: 3804 x 20 / 120 = 634. netProfit 4304-1902-200-480-634 = 1088. Unit cost basis 955.5c; markup x 2 grossed up by 20% tax (1911 x 1.2 = 2293.2), rounded UP to the cent (v1.1): recommended 2294, so item revenue 2294 x 2 = 4588, revenue 5088, tax roundCents(4588 x 20 / 120) = 765, netProfit 5088-1911-200-fees-765 = 1653 (the figures above this note are the pre-rounding-up derivation).

name: hardware-pricing-laborPerUnit-qty2
derivation: The laborPerUnit twin of hardware-pricing-markup-tax-fees-qty2: full $10.00 prep per unit (1000c) instead of the amortized $5.00, which is the only line that moves. perUnitTotal 200+10+0+41+1000+0+200 = 1451; batchTotal 1451x2 = 2902. recommended = resolved = 2902; itemRevenue 2902x2 = 5804, + shipping 500 -> revenue 6304. fees 50 + roundCents(630.4)=630 -> 680. tax = roundCents(5804 x 20 / 120) = roundCents(967.3333) = 967. netProfit 6304-2902-200-680-967 = 1555. Unit cost basis 1455.5c; markup x 2 grossed up by the tax rate and rounded UP to the cent (v1.1): 2911 x 1.2 = 3493.2 -> recommended 3494 (the figures above this note are the pre-rounding-up derivation).

name: failure-negative-rate-floored-consumables
derivation: A failure BUFFER is a cost reserve, never a credit, whichever side of the product is negative. failureRatePct -10 over a positive $2.10 consumables base would be -$0.21; both frozen independent references floor the resulting failure COST at zero and return 0 here. Every other line is untouched: perUnitTotal 200+10+0+0+1000+0 = 1210. Cost valid is false -- a negative rate is still a below-min input error.

name: maxima-batchTotal-saturates
derivation: an executed repro, every input at or below its own documented inclusive maximum and the quote therefore VALID: monthlyFixed 1e9 / monthlyHours 1 x timeHours 1e5 = $1e14 of overhead (1e16 c) on one line; electricity 1e5 h x 1 kW x $0.10 = $10,000 (1000000c); labor $10.00/1e5 = 0c. perUnitTotal = 200 + 1000000 + 1e16 = 10000000001000200. x quantity 1e5 is ~1e21, outside int64 -- it must SATURATE to maxCents, never wrap to a negative total that then gets persisted.

name: maxima-resolvedPrice-times-quantity
derivation: The OTHER unbounded product: resolvedPrice x quantity, with both at their inclusive maxima and the result still exactly inside int64 (so this pins the value, not the clamp). labor $10.00/1e5 = 0c -> perUnitTotal 200+10 = 210; batchTotal 210 x 1e5 = 21000000. salePriceOverride $1e9 resolves to 1e11 c (recommendedPrice is the unit cost basis 210.01c x 2 = 420.02c rounded UP to 421 as of v1.1; it does not feed the override). itemRevenue = 1e11 x 1e5 = 1e16 = revenue. netProfit = 1e16 - 21000000 = 9999999979000000. Batch labor is $10.00 (1000c) rounded once, not 0c per unit x 1e5, so batchTotal is 21001000.

name: maxima-hardware-line-sum
derivation: The third unbounded product the per-field maxima do not cover: the SUM over hardware lines. Each entry is $1e7 x 100000 qty/unit = $1e12 -> 1e14 c (magnitudes kept under 2^53 so the expected total is exact rather than float-rounded). perUnitTotal = 1210 base + 3 x 1e14 = 300000000001210; batchTotal x1 = the same.

name: pricing-markupMultiplier-boundary-1000-valid
derivation: maxMarkupMultiplier is INCLUSIVE, the same shape as marginPct's 99.9 ceiling: 1000 prices. On the 1210c cost basis, recommended = resolved = 1210 x 1000 = 1210000; revenue = same at quantity 1; netProfit = 1210000 - 1210 = 1208790.

name: pricing-markupMultiplier-boundary-10001-invalid
derivation: Just above the inclusive ceiling: pricing is invalid with an above-max markupMultiplier warning, so recommendedPrice stays 0 (the price is never computed for an out-of-range multiplier) and revenue is 0. Cost validity is untouched -- a pricing-only error never blanks the cost totals. netProfit = 0 - batchTotal 1210.

name: pricing-fractional-quantity-salePriceOverride
derivation: docs/formulas.md documents a real batchTotal-vs-itemRevenue divergence at a fractional quantity. Without an override it is unobservable: with no override recommendedPrice is 0 on such a quote, so revenue is 0 either way. An explicit salePriceOverride makes it visible. qty 2.5: labor $10.00/2.5 = $4.00 (400c) -> perUnitTotal 200+10+0+0+400+0 = 610; batchTotal = 610 x 2.5 = 1525 (the RAW fraction). resolvedPrice = toCents($20.00) = 2000; itemRevenue = 2000 x round(2.5) = 2000 x 3 = 6000 (the ROUNDED quantity). netProfit = 6000 - 1525 = 4475. Both cost and pricing are invalid: quantity 2.5 is a not-integer error that cascades.

name: quantity-zero-clamps-to-one
derivation: Quantity 0 is clamped to 1 for the math (docs/formulas.md) and the quote is invalid through the quantity below-min error. Lines: 100 g x $20/kg = 200c, 1 h x 1 kW x $0.10 = 10c, labor $10.00 for the batch = 1000c; perUnitTotal = batchTotal = 1210.

name: quantity-nan-clamps-to-one
derivation: Quantity null (what JSON.stringify(NaN) emits) decodes to NaN, which is clamped to 1 like zero; invalid, same lines as quantity-zero-clamps-to-one.

name: quantity-negative-clamps-to-one
derivation: Negative quantity is clamped to 1 like zero; invalid, same lines as quantity-zero-clamps-to-one.

name: sub-cent-cost-high-quantity
derivation: 0.2 g x $20/kg = $0.004 = 0.4c per unit, which a per-unit cent rounding would drop to 0c and report a $0.00 batch. Extended to the batch in float: 0.4c x 10000 = 4000c ($40.00), rounded once; the displayed per-unit material is round(4000 / 10000) = 0c and perUnitTotal is 0c. The price uses the unrounded unit cost: 0.4 / 0.7 = 0.571c -> 1c. revenue = 1c x 10000 = 10000c; net = 10000 - 4000 = 6000 (60%).

name: pricing-margin-tax-fees-together
derivation: cost 1210c. Margin applies to the pre-tax price: 1210 / 0.75 = 1613.33c; grossed up by 25% tax: x 1.25 = 2016.67 -> 2017c. Fees on revenue 2017: 20 + round(131.105) = 131 + round(60.51) = 61 = 212. Tax carved out of the price-inclusive 2017: round(2017 x 25 / 125) = round(403.4) = 403 (equals the pre-tax 1613.33 x 25% = 403.33). net = 2017 - 1210 - 212 - 403 = 192.

name: pricing-negative-net-profit-valid
derivation: cost 1210c, margin 10% measured on the pre-tax price: 1210 / 0.9 = 1344.44c; grossed up by 25% tax: 1680.56 -> 1681c. Fees: 20 + round(109.265) = 109 + round(50.43) = 50 = 179. Tax round(1681 x 25 / 125) = round(336.2) = 336. net = 1681 - 1210 - 179 - 336 = -44: the quote stays valid and the engine adds a warning-severity net-profit-negative field warning (not asserted by this fixture).

name: failure-rate-89-near-cap
derivation: base 200 + 10 = 210c; failure = 210 x 0.89 / 0.11 = 1699.09 -> 1699c (the linear p x base would be 187c). perUnitTotal = 200 + 10 + 1699 + 1000 = 2909.

name: failure-rate-90-inclusive-max
derivation: base 210c; failure = 210 x 0.9 / 0.1 = 1890c (9x the base). perUnitTotal = 200 + 10 + 1890 + 1000 = 3100. 90 is the inclusive maximum.
